Track 1: A clock is a device people use to tell time. The first known type of clock was the sundial. Over 3500 years ago, people in Egypt and Babylon measured time by observing where shadows from the sun fell across a raised spike in different directions throughout the day. People have also used dripping water, falling sand (in an hour glass), special candles, and even burning incense to keep track of the time. The first known mechanical clocks were made about 800 years ago and were powered by weights; we don't know who built the first one. Many people in England, Italy, and France were thinking about and working on clocks around the same time. Today, clocks come in many shapes and sizes. Some clocks can take up entire towers. Others, called watches, are small enough to be worn on a person’s finger or wrist. Clocks are one of the most commonly used tools around the world!
